origin.description: block() breaks up the i-ndex by period, and then uses that to define the indices to chop x with.
origin.usage: block(x, i, period, every = 1L, origin = NULL)

arguments.name: i
arguments.text: The datetime index to block by. It must match the size of x, be increasing, and contain no missing values.

arguments.name: period
arguments.text: A string defining the period to group by, such as year, month, week, day, hour, or yday.

arguments.name: every
arguments.text: The number of periods to group together.

arguments.name: origin
arguments.text: The reference datetime. The default is 1970-01-01 in the time zone of the index.

origin.details: block() determines the indices to block by with warp::warp_boundary(), and splits x by those indices using vctrs::vec_chop(). Like slide(), block() splits data frame x values row wise.
origin.value: A list with one element per period block. Each element has the same type as x.

translation.description: Breaks x into non-overlapping blocks along a datelike index i and a warp period.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector, NumPy array, column dict, or warp Date / POSIXct / POSIXlt.

arguments.name: i
arguments.text: A warp Date, POSIXct, or POSIXlt index with the same length as x.

translation.details: Calls warp.warp_boundary for start and stop positions, then slices x on each inclusive 1-based range like slider_block in the C code.
translation.value: A list of blocks, each with the same structure as x.
translation.example:
from slider.block import block
from warp import Date
block(i, i, period="year")
